::: {.ter-project-brief}
## Design brief

Measure a related group of real shop tools and create a holder that makes each tool visible, identifiable, accessible, and easy to return. Prototype the critical opening or support before fabricating the complete holder.
:::

## Possible contexts

- Machine shop: drill bits, end mills, collets, precision drivers, or measuring tools.
- Auto shop: sockets, wrenches, screwdrivers, pliers, or pneumatic fittings.
- Woodshop: chisels, files, drill bits, sanding tools, or layout tools.
- Computer engineering/electronics: multimeter leads, soldering tools, tweezers, wire tools, or small drivers.
- General technology shop: markers, hand tools, shared measuring tools, or project kits.

## Design criteria

Measure the actual tools and account for tapers, collars, handles, cords, and the hand position used during removal. Organize repeated geometry deliberately. Provide labels or silhouettes where they improve return-to-home behaviour. Test one-hand removal, visibility, reach, clearance, and whether neighbouring tools collide.

[Browse the purpose-built holder kits](../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/?type=tool-holders#library) for construction ideas. They are unverified starting geometry, not substitutes for measuring the class tools or testing the assembly.

Before an independent holder, complete the [pill-bottle organizer progression](resources/pill-bottle-organizer.qmd). Its four reference systems separate components from examples and make the BOM, interfaces, load path, assembly order and physical-test status visible. Students should be able to explain which pattern transfers to their chosen tool family—and which dimensions do not.

## Required evidence

Include a tool-measurement table, alternatives, selected concept, critical-dimension prototype, user test, revision notes, and a final evaluation against the identified need.

::: {.ter-curriculum-relevance}
**Ontario curriculum relevance:** Particularly useful for **TIJ1O**, **TMJ2O**, **TTJ2O**, and **TCJ2O**. Electronics holders can support **TEJ2O** and senior computer-engineering contexts. Course relevance depends on the actual tools, users, and fabrication process selected.
:::
